title: Tally a large catalogue's tags without losing or doubling any

blocks.text: A marketplace shows how many listings carry each tag ("vegan", "handmade", ...). Small shops' numbers are right. For the large catalogues, which are tallied on a parallel stream, the numbers change from one page load to the next, run into the billions, some are negative, and now and then the tally fails with a `ConcurrentModificationException`.
`TagTally.Counts` keeps one count per tag and is not thread-safe. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/TagTally.java`:

items: `tally(Stream<String>)`: count every tag of the stream into a `Counts`.

blocks.text: The tally must be exact whether its stream is sequential or parallel. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a small catalogue's tags are counted, and adding counts with other tags puts both together
a catalogue large enough to be tallied in parallel gets every tag's exact count
adding counts that share a tag adds the two counts for that tag
a catalogue tallied in parallel keeps every occurrence: the counts add up to the number of tags

origin.section: reduce Combines Values; a Mutable Container Goes Through collect

concepts: collect(supplier, accumulator, combiner) gives each chunk its own container from the supplier, and its combiner must merge two containers fully.
A mutable container passed to reduce as identity is one object shared by every chunk, so a parallel reduce into it loses, duplicates or throws.
